the aging rate in healthy subjects slows down in elderly persons, that it is lower in men than in women, and that it increases in patients with coronary and hypertensive diseases.
the biological age in men is lower than in women, and that aging rate is lower in elderly than in young and middle-aged subjects.

biological age is higher in men and women with coronary heart disease than in healthy subjects of the same age, that biological age is lower in elderly subjects than in younger and middle-aged ones, and that the aging rate is slower in elderly subjects than younger and middle-aged subjects.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a method for determining biological age and aging rates in healthy subjects and in patients with coronary artery disease and hypertensive diseases.
the development of a mathematical model of the biological age of man, and with the study of the factors that influence aging rate.
the development of a method of determining the biological age and the aging rate in man.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the aging process in men is more rapid than in women.
the aging rate is higher in patients with coronary and hypertensive diseases than in healthy persons and in women than in men.
the biological age of a healthy person is lower than the chronological age.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

biological age is a more reliable index for the evaluation of aging rate in man than chronological age, and that it may be used to assess the biological age of the organism in the study of the pathophysiology of aging and the aging-related diseases.
aging rate is an important indicator for the evaluation of biological status in man.
aging is a process of continuous change of the body and mind, but the rate of aging varies among individuals.
The main takeaway from our work is that
aging rate is a more important parameter for the assessment of the biological age than the absolute value of the biological age.
the biological age of an individual is not the same as chronological age, and it can be used to predict the risk of disease.
the aging rate is a useful indicator of aging.
